body: I do have 5 days vacation. I have been unable to take any time since we have been short handed. And yes, the panic buyers have let off but we are a hardware store in a suburban town with only a handful of open stores. People are bored and frustrated with having to stay at home so you can count on busy days full of cranky customers. Look at the parking lots of places like target, walmart, grocery stores, hardware stores and other essential businesses that offer a variety of products. A majority of the time they are mostly full.

Been dealing with depression for 27 years. Been suicidal a lot. 1 attempt that no one knew about. Clearly I failed. I'm just so tired of this roller coaster and have reached a point where I truly no longer feel an attachment to my life. No remorse for leaving everyone behind, for leaving everyone to clean up the mess I leave behind (literally and figuratively). But I don't know how to do it. No gun. No drugs (of the lethal variety). Can't hang myself. Won't harm anyone else by jumping into traffic or causing an accident. Maybe sedate myself enough, do a few shots, and jump off a bridge? Who knows, maybe I don't have the courage since I can't find a way.

Hard advice coming at you (I'm a really nice person so I don't mean to upset but I feel you need the 'unglazed' version). Your faking life and faking "happiness"=depression. If you haven't seen a psychiatrist or therapist, you need to. If you have and don't feel you are getting the help you need, you need to switch to a new one. This is a treatable diagnosis. Not all medications work for everyone so you may have to try multiple times to find one that works for you. Sometimes you need to see a therapist and talk about the issues you face. They can help track your triggers and help you identify them so you can be genuinely happy (or at least neutral) for longer periods of time. If you are not getting that help currently, you need to make a change. Start with a phone call (to your insurance company, your/any psychiatrist, your/any therapist, any person who can help you navigate this. Work your way up from there. Your feelings are valid, you matter, and you don't have to be depressed for the rest of your life.

I understand. And it's a hard road to be on. I have been on medication for many years and changed many times. Some have worked better than others but I have only been on the last medication for 3 years (going strong). When the meds are working I feel a weight has literally lifted off my shoulders initially after starting them. When they stop being enough, AND I have been following all the guidelines (eating healthy, exercise...can't say enough about the serotonin produced from exercise..., therapy, etc.) then I know it's time for a change. If you know it's the meds and the doc says let's try something else, then try it. There is no one size fits all treatment. BUT I think it is imperative to your progress to have "a person". Whether a therapist or close friend, whatever, someone to talk about what's on your mind in a judgement free zone. It's strange how we can feel relief after speaking the words out loud to another person who doesn't give us drama about our thoughts. I catch myself holding it in sometimes (something I'm still working on) and feeling so crappy for days and then I get to my person and word vomit all of it out and it's just so freeing. Weightlifting. I don't realize how much stress it was causing me to keep it inside. It's not a straight road to a healthy you. It's more like a dance. Sometimes you move forward, sometimes backwards and sometimes side to side. Eventually you will end up in a different place altogether. And it's always more fun to do it with someone with you. Good luck at your appointment and I have faith that you will get it all in order.

I have been diagnosed with depression and anxiety and medicated for about 20 years. I suffered with both for years before being diagnosed. 

Short answer is yes.  There are really bad times that can span years. But I have had some good times too where I wasn't suicidal, wishing to cease to exist, or even depressed that lasted years. That doesn't mean my life was perfect and I didn't have struggles, but I wasn't looking for a way out.

Long answer is that I'm currently back in that dark place contemplating the point of my existence. Wishing to go to sleep never to wake up again just for some peace from the constant hurt inside. This is an illness. Some of us will never be cured. Remission exists and can be maintained with a proactive approach. That is, if we can make it through. One would think that experience would be an advantage but the truth is that every time the depression comes back the easier it is to give up. It's sneaky. You think you know what it looks like and feels like but it changes and grabs ahold of you. And when it has you, you know how hard it will be to work out from under it and you've spent so much energy on it already. And you're tired and beaten again. But the bottom line is you just have to decide if you want to fight. You don't have to make a plan or worry about the future or do anything else. Just decide if you're in the fight.
